candidates.topic: Cleopatra's Needle and the hidden time capsule
candidates.teaser: There's a secret box buried under one of New York City's most famous landmarks — and almost no one knows what's inside.
candidates.video_title: What's Hidden Under New York's Ancient Obelisk?
candidates.video_description: The Egyptian obelisk in Central Park holds a Victorian-era time capsule buried beneath it in 1880. It contains some genuinely bizarre items that tell a story about who we were. Nobody talks about this.
candidates.script: There is a 3,500-year-old Egyptian obelisk standing in Central Park right now — and buried beneath it is a sealed metal box that almost nobody knows about. When workers installed it in 1880, they placed a time capsule underneath containing a Bible, a dictionary, a map of New York, coins, and a photo of the men who built it. The obelisk itself is older than the Roman Empire. It stood in Egypt for thousands of years before America even existed. So here's the question — if you had to put one thing in a time capsule today, what would you choose?

candidates.teaser: There's a creature on Earth right now that can survive in outer space, inside a volcano, and at the bottom of the ocean — and it's probably on your skin.
candidates.video_title: The Unkillable Animal Living on Your Body Right Now
candidates.video_description: Tardigrades, also called water bears, are microscopic animals that can survive virtually any condition that would instantly kill every other life form on Earth. They've even been sent to space and came back alive. This is real.
candidates.script: Right now, living on your eyelashes, in soil, and even in Antarctica, there are tiny creatures that are essentially immortal. They're called tardigrades — microscopic animals barely half a millimeter long. Scientists have frozen them for decades, boiled them, exposed them to lethal radiation, and launched them into the vacuum of outer space. They survived all of it. They do this by entering a death-like state where they lose almost all their water and simply pause. They've been around for over 500 million years, surviving five mass extinctions. So whatever ends humanity — these little things will probably still be here. Does that comfort you or terrify you?

candidates.topic: The Placebo Effect is getting stronger over time
candidates.teaser: Fake pills are becoming more powerful every decade — and scientists have no idea why.
candidates.video_title: Why Fake Medicine Is Getting Stronger Every Year
candidates.video_description: The placebo effect — where sugar pills produce real, measurable healing — has been intensifying in clinical trials for decades. Drug companies are struggling to prove their real medicines work better than nothing. The human mind is doing something we can't explain.
candidates.script: Pharmaceutical companies have a growing crisis — their real drugs keep failing trials, not because the drugs got weaker, but because fake pills are getting stronger. The placebo effect, where a sugar pill causes genuine, measurable healing, has been intensifying every decade since the 1980s. In some US pain trials today, placebo beats actual medication over 50% of the time. Scientists think it's connected to how we're conditioned to expect results — the more medical rituals around a treatment, the more powerful the effect. Your brain can literally manufacture pain relief, reduce inflammation, even lower blood pressure — just from belief. So what exactly is the difference between medicine and magic?

candidates.topic: The universe smells like rum and raspberries
candidates.teaser: Astronomers pointed a radio telescope at the center of the Milky Way and accidentally discovered something nobody expected to find in space.
candidates.video_title: Scientists Discovered What Outer Space Actually Smells Like
candidates.video_description: A giant cloud of ethyl formate floating near the center of our galaxy is the same molecule responsible for the flavor of raspberries and the smell of rum. Space has a flavor — and it's surprisingly specific.
candidates.script: In 2009, astronomers scanning the center of our galaxy made one of the strangest discoveries in space history. Hidden in a massive dust cloud near the Milky Way's core, they found ethyl formate — the exact same molecule that gives raspberries their flavor and rum its smell. The cloud is enormous, spanning billions of kilometers. Space, it turns out, isn't just empty and cold — it's full of organic molecules drifting between the stars, including sugars, alcohols, and amino acids, the basic building blocks of life. So the universe doesn't just contain life — it might literally taste like it. If you could smell deep space, would you actually want to?

candidates.topic: The original color of blood — it's always red
candidates.teaser: You've been told your veins look blue because the blood inside them is blue — that's completely false, and the real reason is far stranger.
candidates.video_title: Why Your Veins Look Blue But Blood Is Always Red
candidates.video_description: Many people believe deoxygenated blood is blue — it's even taught in some schools. The truth involves physics, light, and how your skin filters specific wavelengths before they reach your eyes. Blood is never blue inside a living human.
candidates.script: Look at your wrist right now. Those veins look blue — so you've probably heard that blood loses oxygen and turns blue inside your body. That is completely false. Human blood is always red. Even deoxygenated blood in your veins is a dark, deep red. The reason your veins look blue has nothing to do with the blood's color at all — it's about light. Different wavelengths of light penetrate your skin at different depths. Red light passes through deeper, blue light reflects back near the surface — so your eyes only pick up the blue. It's an optical illusion created by your own skin. In surgery, under white light, all blood looks exactly the same — red. So what else about your own body are you seeing completely wrong?
